steps.title: Five on five
steps.body: Two teams of ==five== try to put the ball through the other team's hoop. Pro games are ==four 12-minute quarters==, and the score moves fast.

steps.title: Two points
steps.body: Any basket made from ==inside the arc== is worth 2. That includes layups and dunks right at the rim.

steps.title: Three points
steps.body: Shoot from ==behind the three-point line== and it's worth 3. Both feet have to be behind it: ==a foot on the line makes it a two==.
steps.note: The corner three is the shortest three on the court, so teams love it.

steps.title: Free throws
steps.body: After certain fouls, a player shoots ==free throws== from the line with nobody guarding. Each one made is worth ==1 point==.

steps.title: The shot clock
steps.body: The offense has ==24 seconds== to get off a shot that hits the rim. If time runs out, the ball goes to the ==other team==.
steps.note: Grab an offensive rebound and the clock resets to 14.

steps.title: Score, then defend
steps.body: After a made basket the ==other team inbounds== from under the hoop and attacks the other way. Each team gets ==about 100 possessions== a game.

steps.prompt: How many points is this shot worth?
steps.explain: He let it go with both feet behind the arc, so it's a three.

steps.prompt: A player is fouled, shoots two free throws and makes one. How many points?
steps.explain: Each free throw made is worth 1, so one make is 1 point.
